title: Canonical derived evaluation morphism and its triangle naturality
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the derived internal Hom on the one-object ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and derived tensor computed after K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Put $F_{L,M}(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ and $G_{L,M}(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),M)$. There is a canonical morphism $e_{K,L,M}:F_{L,M}(K)\to G_{L,M}(K)$, the transpose of the composite
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L\longrightarrow M,$$
where the first arrow uses the graded symmetry to evaluate the first and third factors into $L$, and the second is evaluation. It is natural covariantly in $K,M$ and contravariantly in $L$. For fixed $L,M$, both $F_{L,M}$ and $G_{L,M}$ are exact functors of triangulated categories, with the standard signed shift comparisons; $e$ commutes with those comparisons and sends each distinguished triangle in $K$ to a morphism of distinguished triangles, including the square on the connecting map. No invertibility of $e$ is asserted.

source.place: Tags 0A67 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more, signed chain-level construction), and 064J (lemma-derived-tor-exact); RHom exactness in literature/stacks-project/sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated). The compatibility on connecting maps is the signed cone compatibility of this construction.

proof.text: The one-object ringed site with trivial topology is small and its module sheaves are $R$-modules. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] there, and specialize [lem-trf-closed-evaluation-naturality] to its derived closed structure. Its uniquely specified transpose gives $e_{K,L,M}$; its left-uncurrying equation is the composite in the statement. Its three-variable equality gives the required variances, without any finiteness or invertibility assumption.

source.place: Tag 0GWJ, remark-internal-hom-monoidal, item (5) and its two-counit construction; naturality and the left-uncurrying identity are the agent expansion of this construction, also used in more-algebra.tex Tags 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more) and 0A61 (remark-sign-explanation).

proof.text: Choose K-injective representatives $J,I$ of $L,M$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-resolved-model], the canonical derived map of step 1 is exactly $Q(E_P)$ under the isomorphisms $\lambda_P,\rho_P$, where $E_P(h\otimes x)(f)=(-1)^{|x||f|}h(f(x))$. This equality is for the actual unbounded total tensor and product Hom complexes.

source.place: Tags 0A67 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more), and 0A61 (remark-sign-explanation): unbounded resolved representative, finite support in the tensor sum, and identification with the abstract transpose.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-tensor-double-hom-exact-comparisons], $F$ and $G$ are exact with comparisons $\varphi,\psi$ represented by $\tau,\chi$ on these same models, including the connecting-arrow sign. Apply [lem-trf-double-hom-evaluation-shift] to $P,J,I$. Its chain-map identity $\chi_{P,m}E_{P[m]}=E_P[m]\tau_{P,m}$ and the representative equality of step 2 give $\psi_{K,m}e_{K[m],L,M}=e_{K,L,M}[m]\varphi_{K,m}$ in $D(R)$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tags 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more) and 0A61 (remark-sign-explanation), with section-sign-rules: agent expansion of the signed first-variable Hom shifts and the equality (b-m)(c+m)+m(a+b-m+c) = bc+ma modulo 2.

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle $K_1\xrightarrow{u}K_2\xrightarrow{v}K_3\xrightarrow{w}K_1[1]$, step 3 makes both image triangles distinguished. Naturality from step 1 gives the squares for $u,v$ and $G(w)e_3=e_{K_1[1],L,M}F(w)$. Postcompose this last equality by $\psi_{K_1,1}$ and use step 3 to obtain $\psi_{K_1,1}G(w)e_3=e_1[1]\varphi_{K_1,1}F(w)$. This is the connecting square in [def-weil-triangulated-category]; hence the three $e_i$ form the asserted morphism of distinguished triangles.
